title: Unremitted offense would exclude forever; pardon is pure liberality
source_text: XIII. Praeterea, inquit, quaelibet offensa Dei nisi remitteretur, repelleret a gloria Dei perpetuo, & absque termino puniretur. Alioqui maneret dedecus culpae sine decore justitiae. Quod autem offensa dimittitur, aut remittitur, est ex pura liberalitate Dei remittentis, & non amplius imputantis. Denique non minus est fugibilis offensa Dei, quam sit eligibile illud bonum, pro quo adipiscendo nullo modo deberet committi. Sed pro infinito bono non debet fieri offensa Dei. Et si quis infinita bona possideret, posset juste omnibus a Deo spoliari, si caderet in offensam Dei.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, he says, any offense of God, unless it were remitted, would drive forever from the glory of God and would be punished without end. Otherwise the disgrace of guilt would remain without the beauty of justice. But that an offense is dismissed or remitted is from the pure liberality of God remitting and no longer imputing. Finally, an offense of God is no less to be fled than that good is to be chosen for the obtaining of which it ought in no way to be committed. But for an infinite good an offense of God ought not to be done. And if someone possessed infinite goods, he could justly be stripped of them all by God if he fell into an offense of God.
pass_b_english: Without remission, any offense would forever bar glory and never stop being punished.
Pardon is pure liberality; infinite goods still cannot justify offending God.

choices.why: Pardon as free gift, not owed mildness of the act.
